episodes.169325: Despite an early onset to the year's monsoon season and significant June rainfall totals, flash flooding and debris flow had not been reported across the largest burn scar in New Mexico likely thanks to steady, stratiform rain that had been occurring since mid-June. However, a more traditional monsoon pattern finally set up on July 1, 2022 as the high pressure to the east of New Mexico allowed for a deep plume of monsoonal moisture. Thunderstorms that developed over the Hermits Peak and Calf Canyon burn area were now more convective and prone to producing heavy rainfall rates. This caused the most significant flash flooding so far of the season as multiple reports of flooding and debris flow across the burn scar were received. This prompted evacuations and road closures across western Mora and San Miguel counties.
episodes.169341: A severe thunderstorm developed in southern Saskatchewan and crossed south of the border into Montana.  Daniels, Sheridan and Roosevelt Counties were impacted before the storm weakened and moved out of the area.
episodes.169342: A trough over the Pacific Northwest sent a shortwave up and over an upper level ridge parked over central Montana.  This would set off a round of severe thunderstorms during the afternoon hours.
episodes.169354: With a deep plume of moisture focused across western and central New Mexico, another active monsoon day occurred on July 2, 2022. Thunderstorms first initiated along the mountainous terrain with steering flow tracking this activity in a northerly to northeasterly direction. Several thunderstorms that developed near the Hermits Peak and Calf Canyon burn scar produced an estimated 0.75 to 1.25 inches along the northern half of the burn scar. That resulted in flash flooding and debris flow along Highway 94 near Ledoux.
episodes.169382: As deep layer moisture increased ahead of an approaching cold front on July 1, 2022, low level convergence on the leading edge of moisture advection coincided with lift associated with the right entrance region of a 95KT upper jet. The result was multiple clusters of thunderstorms moving across the southern half of central PA through the afternoon, several of which produced isolated areas of straight line wind damage. Another line of convection developed closer to the cold front during the evening in NW Pennsylvania and moved southeastward, producing isolated straight line wind damage until about 1:00 AM EDT on July 2. The downburst potential was enhanced by a layer of dry air in the environment above 750 hPa, which resulted in DCAPE values of 1200-1300 J/kg through the day and into the evening hours.
episodes.169383: As an upper trough moved eastward into New England on July 2, 2022, the eastern half of Pennsylvania remained in the right entrance region of the trough, promoting weak ascent in the atmosphere. A cold front slowly moved southeastward across Pennsylvania, with a prefrontal trough over the lower Susquehanna Valley acting as a primary trigger for afternoon convection. Several discrete and multicell thunderstorms developed within a narrow corridor around the prefrontal trough, in an environment with 2000 J/kg CAPE and up to 1200 J/kg of DCAPE. Deep layer 0-6 km shear of up to 35 kts combined with the instability to promote briefly rotating updrafts with transient supercell characteristics for at least one thunderstorm, which produced ping pong ball size hail. There were also several reports of damaging straight line winds associated with downbursts.
episodes.169387: A cold front was slowly pushing through the state on Saturday, July 2. Warm and humid conditions ahead of the front led to destabilization, and the development of strong storms with excessive rain and frequent cloud to ground lightning. Several of these storms out-preformed the rest, with higher cores and stronger winds. This resulted in four severe thunderstorm warnings being issued throughout the evening across southeast Kentucky. Unfortunately, only one of these storms actually resulted in realized severe winds at the surface, near Jackson in Breathitt County.
episodes.169392: A cold front dropped down from the north, causing showers and thunderstorms to develop. The storm motion was nearly parallel to the boundary, causing some storms to train over the same area. This led to instances of flooding and flash flooding.
episodes.169498: A shortwave trough moving eastward from the eastern Great Lakes, triggered strong thunderstorms in New York state, which moved into southern New England overnight.  The atmosphere was very unstable and surface dewpoints were near 70 degrees. The result was strong to locally severe thunderstorms before daybreak.
episodes.169499: A shortwave trough moving eastward from the eastern Great Lakes, triggered strong thunderstorms in New York state, which moved into southern New England overnight.  The atmosphere was very unstable and surface dewpoints were near 70 degrees. The result was strong to locally severe thunderstorms before daybreak.
episodes.169500: A shortwave trough moving eastward from the eastern Great Lakes, triggered strong thunderstorms in New York state, which moved into southern New England overnight.  The atmosphere was very unstable and surface dewpoints were near 70 degrees. The result was strong to locally severe thunderstorms before daybreak in southeast MA.  Sunshine boosted temperatures in the afternoon, then a cold front swept through in the evening hours, triggering a second round of strong to severe thunderstorms, mainly in western and central MA.
episodes.169524: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms developed over southwestern South Dakota and tracked east-southeast into south central South Dakota. The storms produced wind gusts over 60 mph.
episodes.169526: A thunderstorm briefly became severe over the west side of Rapid City, producing some hail to quarter size.
episodes.170076: A few isolated severe thunderstorms occurred across the Billings Forecast Area.
episodes.170319: A surface cold front drifted southeastward across northern Indiana, southeast Lower Michigan, southern Ontario, and into northwest Ohio during the afternoon through early evening of the 1st. Simultaneously, a pre-frontal surface trough axis in the warm sector moved generally eastward across northern Ohio and Lake Erie. Low-level convergence and ascent along the pre-frontal trough axis acted as a focus for the development of multicellular showers and thunderstorms amidst weak to moderate MUCAPE and moderate to strong DCAPE and effective bulk shear, respectively. Some of the multicell storms produced isolated straight-line wind damage.
episodes.170511: A small cluster of strong to severe thunderstorms developed along a weak cold front as it pushed southeast across western Kentucky. A few of the storms produced wind gusts around 60 mph. A slow-moving thunderstorm caused isolated flash flooding of an urban area.
episodes.170600: A few severe thunderstorms produced several instances of wind damage ahead of a cold front during the afternoon and evening hours.
episodes.170601: A few severe thunderstorms produced several instances of wind damage ahead of a cold front during the afternoon and evening hours.
episodes.170602: A few severe thunderstorms produced several instances of wind damage ahead of a cold front during the afternoon and evening hours.
episodes.170887: A pair of thunderstorms passed over Rock Springs during the afternoon and evening. High winds occurred at the Sweetwater County Airport to the east of Rock Springs. No damage was reported.
episodes.170904: A strong shortwave moved through Central New York and kicked off numerous lines of continuously developing thunderstorms. Many of these thunderstorms became severe, knocking down trees in several towns across Central New York.
episodes.170905: A strong shortwave moved through Northeast Pennsylvania and kicked off scattered thunderstorms. A couple of these thunderstorms became severe with damaging winds and large hail.
episodes.170949: Trade wind showers fell over northern and windward portions of the Big Island. The rain produced small steam and drainage ditch flooding, and ponding on the roadways. No serious injuries or property damage were reported.
episodes.171048: As a cold front progressed eastward through the Ohio Valley on the 2nd of July, strong to severe thunderstorms ensued. Daytime heating continued to tack on the potential for these strong storms, which became evident by that evening as active weather charged into West Virginia.||Main impacts from these strong storms were noted in the western lowlands where tree damage occurred, as did sub-severe hail in Boone County.
episodes.171092: Scattered thunderstorms developed across the region producing isolated areas of wind damage and hail across the area. One storm impacted portions of Monmouth County and another isolated storm produced a 50 kt wind gust in Cumberland County.
episodes.171095: Scattered thunderstorms developed across the region producing isolated areas of wind damage and hail across the area. Training cells produced a couple instances of tree damage in southern Chester County in addition to heavy rainfall resulting in some localized flooding.
episodes.171174: The region was between a weak coastal low to the NNE and a surface high pressure ridge axis stretching from near Bermuda into central FL. Tropical airmass is in place with precipitable water amounts of 2 inches allowing storms to produce heavy rainfall. The Atlantic coast sea breeze was pinned to the coast as the Gulf sea breeze moved inland through the afternoon. The sea breezes converged along the I-95 corridor in the late afternoon. Heavy downpours and slow storm motion led to localized flash and urban flooding in downtown Jacksonville.
episodes.171270: Strong to severe thunderstorms erupted along a slow moving cold front over southern WI. Large hail, damaging winds, and flash flooding occurred. A lightning strike and subsequent fire caused significant damage to a home in Beloit.
episodes.171314: A cold front crossed the region during the 2nd. Thunderstorms developed across Downeast areas during the afternoon in the warm humid air in advance of the front. An isolated severe thunderstorm produced large hail along the coast of Hancock county.
episodes.171399: Severe thunderstorms initiated near a surface low and weak frontal zone in northeast Montana. The storms then moved into western North Dakota, spreading south along the front, while the whole complex move towards the southeast. Strong wind gusts were the main threats with these storms, with the strongest reported wind gust of 82 mph occurring in Slope County. One-inch diameter hail occurred in Mountrail and McLean counties.
episodes.171539: A cluster of slow-moving thunderstorms developed along a cold front during the evening, producing isolated wind damage and flash flooding south of I-70.
episodes.171789: An MCV moved across southern Missouri during the day on July 2nd. Numerous showers and storms developed as it moved east across the region. Some of the storms became severe producing damaging winds.
episodes.171813: Severe thunderstorms formed ahead of an approaching cold front and moved over the waters. The storms produced severe wind gusts.
episodes.171948: Clusters of strong to severe thunderstorms along and ahead of an approaching cold front from the west resulted in a few damaging wind reports including a few downed trees and wires across eastern New York Friday night July 1, 2022.
episodes.171950: A line of strong to severe storms resulted in a couple of downed trees near Litchfield CT Saturday evening July 2, 2022.
episodes.172023: A weak upper low pressure system teamed with moisture from a remnant tropical low to bring widely scattered afternoon and evening thunderstorms to the region in the first few days of July. Minor wind damage associated with these storms was reported in a few isolated locations.
episodes.172030: A line of afternoon storms formed ahead of an approaching cold front. This line produced a few instances of wind damage across southeast West Virginia in a moderately unstable atmosphere.
episodes.172031: A line of afternoon storms formed ahead of an approaching cold front. This line produced a few instances of wind damage across southwest Virginia in a moderately unstable atmosphere.
episodes.172032: A line of afternoon storms formed ahead of an approaching cold front. This line produced localized damaging winds in Surry County in moderately unstable atmosphere.
episodes.172105: An active tropical wave moved across the area. This wave brought periods of heavy rainfall, along with strong gusty winds, resulting in multiple flood reports.
episodes.172114: A severe thunderstorm produced 1.00 inch diameter hail while moving offshore across Frenchman Bay along the Downeast coast.
episodes.172144: A line of mostly sub-severe thunderstorms preceded a cold front during the evening hours of July 1st.  Only one instance of wind damage was noted in Armstrong County.
episodes.172184: Scattered thunderstorms developed across northern Oklahoma during the afternoon of the 2nd, with an isolated report of large hail received.
episodes.172199: Scattered thunderstorms developed across parts of southern Colorado late in the day and into the evening. The strongest storms occurred across Pueblo County, where damaging winds up to 65 mph and heavy rainfall with localized flash flooding occurred.
episodes.172237: An isolated supercell thunderstorm developed along a a stalled cold front across central Kansas.  The supercell produced half dollar size hail and 60 mph winds.
episodes.172368: During the late morning and afternoon hours of July 2nd, clusters of showers and thunderstorms developed along and south of a quasi-stationary frontal boundary which was draped from west to east across Kentucky. South of the boundary, warm and humid conditions in the low levels contributed to sufficient instability for the development of thunderstorms. The most favorable environmental shear was offset from the greatest instability, limiting the overall severe threat, with only one wind damage report observed in Butler County.
episodes.172564: Scattered thunderstorms developed across the Texas Panhandle during the late afternoon and evening of the 2nd. A couple of these storms became severe in the areas due to instability present which resulted in wind gusts.
episodes.172566: A severe weather outbreak main affected the Upper Snake River Plain with rrports of greater than 50 knot winds, large hail and lightning strikes.
episodes.172673: Scattered thunderstorms moved west across southeast Arizona from mid morning through early evening. A couple of storms downed trees and produced flash flooding in the Tucson Metro area.
episodes.172764: Scattered thunderstorms developed over the southern Appalachians during the afternoon. One of the storms resulted in a lightning fatality in the Mountain City area, while another storm produced damaging wind gusts near Clayton.
episodes.172836: An upper low in the eastern Pacific guided a moisture plume over the region, resulting in numerous rain showers developing across the region. Increasing instability from southerly flow aloft also resulted in thunderstorms developing, with a few storms producing hail stones over an inch in diameter, strong winds, and brief heavy downpours.
episodes.173037: Aided by a weak disturbance moving off the Georgia coast, showers and thunderstorms developed within an abnormally moist tropical airmass along converging outflow boundaries. These pulse convective storms produced isolated reports of trees and powerlines down in west-central Georgia.
